title: Generative design leads to a synthesized magnesium-based thermoelectric composition
summary: A generative model combining a variational autoencoder, residual layers and discriminators proposed thermoelectric compositions from literature-derived data. Researchers synthesized the selected Mg 3.1 Sb 0.5 Bi 1.497 Te 0.003 composition and reported a thermoelectric figure of merit of 0.75 at 300 kelvin. This laboratory measurement is separate from the larger catalogue of predicted high-performance materials; it does not establish that all predictions were synthesized or that this room-temperature sample exceeded a figure of merit of 1.
ai_technology: Variational autoencoder; residual neural network; learned discriminators
organization: Harbin Institute of Technology; Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: The official supporting TableS 7 explicitly marks Mg 3.1 Bi 1.497 Sb 0.5 Te 0.003 as synthesized in this study and reports its transport properties and thermoelectric figure of merit of 0.75 at 300 kelvin.
evidence.unknown: Broad experimental success across the predicted catalogue, independent replication and practical device benefit remain unestablished. The reported 100 materials above a predicted figure of merit of 1 are computational candidates, not 100 newly tested materials.
evidence.ai_role: A conditional generative architecture learns composition/property relationships using a variational encoder-decoder with residual layers, discriminators and a diversity-related loss, generating candidate compositions for experimental selection.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher front metadata and abstract, complete official supporting information model architecture and measured-versus-predicted tables, plus current PubMed notice metadata. Paywalled main article body was not read; no independent replication performed.
